subsystem.name: measurement
subsystem.note: The G6 harness, interlock tests/measurement, 14 files. One ledger per source file. fixtures is the fifth file of this lane and the largest; it is also the first to carry DATA rather than only code -- the labelled corpus at test/fixtures/labelled/, byte-identical to interlock's tests/fixtures/labelled/.

carried_data.verification: Byte-identical (`diff -r` clean), and -- the stronger check -- interlock's own load_corpus run against BOTH trees produces the same content digest, 1b498122287a8443e6a259ecf9904fe8bc90c517dbfa588dfae176e595b18847. A target-only test pins that value, so the two halves it proves (the files arrived unaltered, and this port's digest construction agrees with the source's) cannot drift apart silently.
carried_data.protection: Two ways it could rot were closed rather than left to luck: biome.json now excludes test/fixtures/labelled/** and parity/oracle/** from formatting (a reflowed JSON file changes the digest), and .gitattributes already pins eol=lf globally (a CRLF checkout would too).

systematic_mappings.to: parametrize() with pytest's ids written out
systematic_mappings.why: Rule 2 of docs/test-translation-conventions.md. Five parametrized source cases expand to 21 of the 59 node ids ([trace.jsonl], the seven LABEL_FIELDS, three window fields, six overridesN, six trace ids), and each expansion is its own ledger row. The LABEL_FIELDS one is parametrized over the module's own exported constant, exactly as the source is, so a field added to the table is covered the day it is added.
D-0104: toFixed and Python's .2f disagree on exact ties, and a rate is count/count. An implementation change, not a test change.
systematic_mappings.affects: the rendered rate lines; no entry's assertion changed

target_only_tests.note: Target-only tests translate no source case and are NOT counted as ported coverage. This one is the parity evidence for the carried DATA rather than for code: it pins the corpus content digest to the value interlock's own loader produces over interlock's own tree, which proves both that the files arrived unaltered and that this port's digest construction (id, NUL, filename, NUL, bytes, NUL, over cases sorted by id) agrees with the source's. Interlock has no such test because it has only one copy of the corpus and nothing to compare against. Six more close properties a 36-mutation sweep found unguarded; each is recorded with its verdict under mutation_sweep below. Five are inherited (interlock's suite cannot tell the mutated module from the real one either, verified against 65f36c5 in each case) and one is a port artifact. Production behaviour is unchanged throughout. Three more were added after the codex review gate found three PORT DIVERGENCES (not inherited gaps) in the same pass: the corpus walk sorted by UTF-16 code unit where Python sorts by code point, the composition map was borrowed rather than copied, and the earliest-alarm minimum spread an unbounded array into Math.min. All three are fixed in the module and pinned here.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: The corpus refuses to load without at least one negative AND one positive case, so a corpus cannot be grown one case at a time from empty -- the first two cases must arrive together.
inherited_limitations.note: Deliberate upstream: the arithmetic is the argument. A positive-only corpus scores a perfect miss rate for a detector that alarms on everything, and a negative-only one scores a perfect false-positive rate for a detector that alarms on nothing. The friction is the point and is recorded so it is not mistaken for a bug.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: The grader runs no detector. It reads a caller-supplied map of case id to produced incidents, so nothing here verifies that the incidents were produced by replaying the trace at all.
inherited_limitations.note: Structural upstream and reproduced: the module loads and grades and explicitly does not run detectors. The one property it CAN enforce about the detector's honesty -- that every instant came from the injected clock -- it does enforce, and refuses anything else (ClockNotSynthetic).
inherited_limitations.where_a_fix_belongs: upstream, in whatever eventually drives the replay; out of scope for the parity port by interlock#74 acceptance criterion 6.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: Five properties of the loader and grader are unguarded by interlock's own suite: the budget_ms minimum (shadowed by the T > L rule), the upfront-versus-interleaved clock check (the source's case for it cannot discriminate), the null-versus-zero empty-denominator rate, nearest-rank percentiles, and the rate formatter.
inherited_limitations.note: Found by a 36-mutation sweep on the port and verified against interlock 65f36c5 case by case. The port reproduces the production behaviour exactly and does not change it; it adds five target-only tests so the properties stop being unguarded on this side. The clock one is the notable entry: interlock HAS a case for it whose docstring states the hazard precisely, and the case cannot detect it because the corpus's sort order grades the stamped case first.
inherited_limitations.where_a_fix_belongs: upstream, as the same five cases added to interlock's tests/measurement/test_fixtures.py.

entries.reason: The source asserts only `pytest.raises(Exception)`, which any error satisfies. The port names the type the module actually raises (EvaluationRefusal), which is strictly STRONGER: a different error would pass upstream and fails here. Recorded as adapted rather than ported because a reviewer comparing the two sees a narrower assertion and should find the reason here, not reconstruct it.

entries.reason: The source asserts ASCII twice, by encoding the rendered text to cp932 AND to ascii -- the cp932 encode is the one that reproduces the Japanese-console crash a UTF-8 pytest capture never sees. JavaScript has no cp932 encoder and needs none: ASCII is a strict SUBSET of cp932, so `isAscii(text)` implies both source assertions and neither is weakened. Every other assertion in the case is unchanged.

mutation_sweep.ran: 36 mutations, one per property the ported cases claim to pin, 2026-08-22

survivors.mutation: parseLabel drops the 'missing required field(s)' check
survivors.verdict: PORT ARTIFACT, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: In Python the next line raises KeyError -- a different type -- so the seven ported cases fail. In TypeScript a missing key reads as `undefined`, flows into that field's own type check, and produces a LabelMalformed naming the same field, so the seven pass either way. The check still earns its place: it names ALL missing fields at once and cites section 3.2, where the downstream checks report only the first. That wording is what the new case pins.

survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: The ported case drives budget_ms=0 but asserts only LabelMalformed, and with the minimum lowered the refusal still fires -- via tolerance_ms=180000 > budget_ms=0. Interlock's case is identical. The new case sets T=0 so the T > L rule cannot fire and only the minimum can.

survivors.mutation: evaluate checks clock instants interleaved with grading instead of all upfront
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test -- and the source's own case for it does not work
survivors.note: interlock has test_one_cases_minting_cannot_vouch_for_another, whose docstring states this hazard exactly, and it cannot detect it: it puts the foreign stamp on the NEGATIVE case, and load_corpus sorts by directory, so observation_unavailable is graded FIRST and nothing has minted anything by the time it is checked. Verified against interlock 65f36c5 -- the same corpus yields the same order there. The discriminator needs two POSITIVE cases, so that grading the first mints the instant the second's foreign stamp uses.

survivors.mutation: missRate / falsePositiveRate return 0 instead of null on an empty denominator
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: Unreachable through loadCorpus, which refuses a corpus with no positives or no negatives -- but FixtureEvaluation is exported and a caller can build one, and interlock's is equally reachable and equally untested. The distinction is the module's own stated design: printing 0.00 for a rate over zero cases is the harness claiming a result it has no cases to support.

survivors.mutation: the latency percentile interpolates instead of using nearest rank
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: The shipped-corpus report case detects every positive at the same 45 s, so a percentile over identical values is identical under either rule; interlock's sample is the same. The new case uses three distinct latencies, where nearest-rank p90 is the 3rd smallest and interpolation returns a value no detection exhibited.

survivors.mutation: the rate helper uses toFixed instead of formatFixed
survivors.verdict: inherited liveness gap, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: The same shape as the one closed in the false-termination belt: D-0104's oracle proves formatFixed correct but not that this module calls it, and no ported case drives a rate to an exact tie. The new case makes the miss rate 1/8 = 0.125, where CPython prints 0.12 and toFixed prints 0.13.

survivors.mutation: (codex review, not the sweep) sort order, composition copy, spread minimum
survivors.verdict: three PORT DIVERGENCES, all fixed and pinned
survivors.note: Found by the review gate rather than by the sweep, and worth recording beside it because they are the class the sweep is worst at: a mutation list asks 'is this property tested', and these are places where the port silently did something Python does not. (1) JavaScript's `<` and default sort compare UTF-16 code units, Python compares code points; they disagree for every supplementary character, and the corpus digest is taken over cases in SORTED order -- so the cross-runtime digest identity this belt claims was true only for BMP names. `comparePythonStrings` in src/measurement/format.ts now backs every string sort in fixtures.ts and latency.ts. (2) `composition` was assigned from the caller's Map rather than copied, so a caller could set a new denominator into a published evaluation. (3) `Math.min(...array)` throws past roughly a hundred thousand elements where Python's min() has no ceiling, so a noisy detector would crash this harness and not interlock's.
